summary:
Round 9, doc-only. NO ASSERTION WAS WEAKENED: nothing under format/src/test or any other test path moved since round 8 -- the only file touched is docs/internal/product/backlog.md, and SubscriptionEventGrantTest's predicates including .contains("byteStart=4096")/.contains("byteLen=65536") are byte-identical for the fourth round running.

BOTH OF MY ROUND-8 MAJORS ARE CLOSED AND I TRIED TO REOPEN EACH. (1) The boundary pair is now two-sided -- 'at K = crossover, exactly TWO requests and fewer bytes than the whole-object GET; at K = crossover + 1, exactly ONE request and exactly the whole-object bytes'. nodeRunCount <= 1 now reds the K = crossover arm (it would take whole-object there: one request, whole-object bytes, not 'exactly TWO and fewer'), and nodeRunCount <= crossover + 1 reds the other arm. Both single-sided boundary flips of the intended `K <= crossover` are killed, which is what a two-sided pair is for. I also re-checked the open-ended `bytes=byteStart-` shape the bytes-bounded-above clause was added for: at K = 169 it fetches 78,400 + objLen*169/170 = 8,417,672 > 8,388,608, so it now reds 'fewer bytes' at the crossover as well. (2) The M5.45h dependency landed with the local-driver discharge named ('reports 2 where production reports 170 and 1 where production reports 400'), and the 1,556 figure is re-attributed to R12's byte-to-GET conversion with a tight union, which is arithmetically the right home for it. The cross-AZ arm is withdrawn consistently now -- the clause and the figures agree.

CRITERION 2 BREAKS AN EIGHTH TIME, AND THE BREAK IS CREATED BY THIS ROUND'S OWN EDIT. Moving the low side of the pair up from K = 1 to K = crossover removed the only assertion site below the switch point, so 1 <= K < crossover is now wholly unasserted -- and the M5.45h dependency declared in the same edit makes that region actively contradictory rather than merely uncovered. M5.45h criterion 1 asserts ONE fetch at K = 64 through the node's client owner with a fake that 'COUNTS INVOCATIONS, NOT DISTINCT URLS'; M5.66 lands after it and, if its threshold really is the recorded crossover (169 on dollars, 213 on bandwidth, 1,556 on the tight union -- every figure this row records is above 64), makes that identical K = 64 path issue TWO invocations of the widened seam, the total across fetchDirectory and fetchRange that criterion 2 itself insists on. So either M5.45h's ONE-fetch assertion is loosened to two in M5.66's commit -- testing.md rule 5 and non-negotiable 2, authorised by no criterion here -- or the bounded path is NOT taken at K = 64, in which case the threshold is not the recorded crossover and criterion 1's derivedFrom requirement is discharged at one K. Detail and the surviving implementation below.

No other implementation satisfying the remaining criteria is still wrong as far as I can find: the RTT predicate remains symmetric and false for both sequential orders, 3b still reds the reader.find() substitution, and the codec-refuse arm still reds decodeRun(wholeSegment, ...). The fix here is one more asserted share, below the crossover, plus one sentence saying what K = 64 does.

findings.title: Moving the low side of the pair from K = 1 up to K = crossover left 1 <= K < crossover with no asserted request count at all -- and the M5.45h dependency declared in the same edit makes K = 64 contradictory, not merely uncovered: M5.45h asserts ONE invocation there and criterion 2's threshold makes it two
findings.failure_scenario:
TWO LIMBS, ONE CAUSE. LIMB 1 -- SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION, and a natural one rather than a contrived one, because it is literally what doc 10 section 7 prescribes ('merge adjacent ranges') and what M5.45h is named for. Correct code is `if (nodeRunCount <= crossover) { header + unionSlice(ranges) } else { wholeObjectGet() }`. Swap one call site: `unionSlice(ranges)` becomes `coalesce(ranges, GAP_LIMIT)`, issuing one GET per coalesced group -- the conventional S3 read-coalescing shape, with GAP_LIMIT a conventional 64 KiB. Walk criterion 2's enumerated cases. 1,600 runs over 8 MiB is ~5,243 bytes per run, and K runs spread through a (indexId, partitionId)-sorted segment sit ~(1600/K) runs apart. At K = crossover = 169 the gap is 9.47 runs = ~49,650 bytes < 64 KiB, so every group merges into ONE slice: exactly TWO requests, bytes = 78,400 + objLen*168/170 = 8,368,319 < 8,388,608, fewer than the whole-object GET. GREEN. At K = crossover + 1 = 170: whole-object path, exactly ONE request, exactly the whole-object bytes. GREEN. At ~400: whole-object, one request, no more bytes. GREEN. Bytes bounded above -- header plus sum of byteLen plus a stated constant -- GREEN at every one of them, and green at K = 64 too where the coalescing path fetches only 78,400 + 335,552 = ~414 KB, i.e. it looks BETTER on the bytes arm. The RTT clause is green at the crossover (both requests issued before either response). 3b is green. The codec-refuse fixture is green. And at K = 64 -- the gap is 25 runs = ~131,072 bytes > GAP_LIMIT, nothing merges -- it issues 65 REQUESTS AGAINST 1. That is runs-per-node scaling, which non-negotiable 6 forbids by name, at the exact share M5.45h calls the realistic one, switched on just below the only K anyone asserts. The clause 'AT MOST TWO REQUESTS AT EVERY K' mandates the property but names its assertion sites only at the crossover and above, and this row's own standard for that is written three cells away: M5.45h demands its residency bound be 'NAMED AND ASSERTED, not merely budgeted in prose' and says a 'stated-only criterion cannot' tell the two failure shapes apart. Same defect, same row family.

LIMB 2, AND THIS ONE IS NEW THIS ROUND BECAUSE THE DEPENDENCY IS NEW THIS ROUND. The unasserted region is not free: M5.45h criterion 1 already asserts into it. backlog.md:69 reads 'a node holding K runs of one segment issues ONE fetch AND ALL K RUNS DECODE THEIR OWN RECORDS FROM IT, asserted at K = 64 ON ONE NODE through whatever holds that node's clients', with 'THE FAKE COUNTS INVOCATIONS, NOT DISTINCT URLS'. M5.66 now depends on M5.45h, so M5.45h lands first and that case exists. Every crossover figure M5.66 records is above 64 -- 169 on dollars, 213 on bandwidth alone, 1,556 on R12's byte-to-GET conversion with a tight union -- so under the intended `K <= crossover` threshold the bounded path IS taken at K = 64 and the node's owner invokes the widened seam TWICE. Criterion 2 forbids counting only one method on it ('a widened seam with fetchRange and fetchDirectory beside each other lets a fake count fetchRange and miss the directory fetch entirely ... the assertion is on the TOTAL'), so the total M5.45h's fake reads goes from 1 to 2 and its criterion-1 case reds. The owner then has exactly two ways out, and criterion 2 authorises neither: (a) loosen M5.45h's ONE-fetch assertion to two in M5.66's commit -- an existing assertion weakened alongside the production change that needed it weakened, testing.md rule 5 and non-negotiable 2, and invisible to check-test-integrity because it is a different row's test being edited to fit; or (b) keep whole-object at K = 64, which means the threshold is NOT the recorded crossover, criterion 1's 'THE CODE'S THRESHOLD IS DERIVED FROM THE RECORDED NUMBER, NOT MERELY COMPARED TO IT' is discharged at the single K the pair pins, and limb 1's implementation becomes the specified one rather than a mutation of it.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE BOTH, at the cost of one case and one sentence: (i) assert the request count at a third share BELOW the crossover -- K = 64, the share M5.45h already uses -- as exactly TWO, so 'at most two at every K' has an assertion site in the region where per-run and partial-coalescing scaling lives; and (ii) say in this cell what K = 64 does to M5.45h's ONE-fetch assertion -- either that M5.66 restates it as one fetch per node across two invocations and why that is a correction rather than a loosening, or that the bounded path is bounded below as well as above and M5.45h's case is untouched. Whichever is chosen, the cell that creates the collision is the cell that owes the answer.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, twice: 'per-node residency is M5.45h's and this row has no dependency, so it may land first' and 'M5.45h's K = 64 case does not backstop it: this row has no dependency and may land first')
findings.title: Criterion 2 still rests two of its clauses on 'this row has no dependency', which the State cell in the same edit reverses -- the half-landed fix this row names as its own recurring shape
findings.failure_scenario: The State cell now reads 'todo -- depends on M5.45g and M5.45h' and spends a paragraph saying the earlier refusal was made on the wrong ground. Criterion 2 was not swept for the claim the State cell just retired, so it asserts the opposite twice, and in both places the retired claim is load-bearing FOR THE CLAUSE IT INTRODUCES: 'M5.45h's K = 64 case does not backstop it: this row has no dependency and may land first' is the stated reason the total-at-the-seam assertion is needed. next-task sends M5.66's owner to this cell before the ADR and before the State column, so the first thing they read is that M5.45h's case is unavailable to them -- which is now false, and which is the premise limb 1 of my major turns on. The conclusions of both clauses (count every request the path makes, take the assertion on the total) survive the correction unchanged, which is why this is minor and not part of the major: no assertion is weakened by it. It is the pattern this row names about itself -- 'the half-landed fix this task has now produced six times' -- one more time, and the cheapest repair is to strike the four words in both places rather than re-argue either clause.
